# Israel crosses Iran’s Lebanon red lines as Tehran leans on maritime leverage

![Ata Mohamed Tabriz](https://i.iranintl.com/images/rdk9umy0/production/9be3926bbc747f298d5dbc60d40cac25210182d4-524x504.jpg?rect=10,0,504,504&w=96&h=96&q=58&fit=max&sat=-100&auto=format)

[Ata Mohamed Tabriz](https://www.iranintl.com/en/author/ata-mohamed)

Iran analyst

Israel’s destruction of Hezbollah’s underground complex at Ali al-Taher, despite Iranian warnings against a major assault there, has exposed the limits of Tehran’s deterrence in Lebanon.

Israeli forces said they established operational control above and below the strategic ridge before demolishing more than two kilometers of tunnels used by Hezbollah’s Badr unit. The operation crossed a red line Tehran had explicitly drawn, but Iran has so far avoided opening a new front in response.

Instead, Tehran is increasingly relying on maritime pressure as a source of leverage. The Strait of Hormuz gives Iran a tool independent of Hezbollah’s weakened position in Lebanon, while recent Houthi advances around Bab al-Mandeb have strengthened another Iran-aligned pressure point along a major global shipping route.

The developments point to an increasingly uneven map of Iranian influence: shrinking deterrence in Lebanon, but continued capacity to impose wider costs through strategic waterways.

# The U.S. has made progress in reopening the Strait of Hormuz, but the Iran war is far from over

In recent weeks, the United States has succeeded in loosening Iran's grip over the Strait of Hormuz while virtually shutting down Iran's own oil exports, accelerating its economic free fall.

But the war launched by the U.S. and Israel in February — intended to last a few weeks — is still far from over, and the stalemate is costly for both sides. An agreement reached in June quickly crumbled, with no sign of diplomatic progress since then. Low-level fighting persists, and the U.S. does not seem to have an exit strategy.

# **Russian losses in the war with Ukraine.** Mediazona count, updated

*Mediazona*, working with the *BBC’s* Russian service and a team of volunteers, has been compiling and maintaining a named list of the Russian military dead. The list is built from publicly available, verifiable sources, such as social media posts by relatives, reports in local media, and statements from regional authorities. Of course, this list is not exhaustive, as not every death is publicly reported.

To build a more complete picture of the war’s true toll, we have developed an estimate based on excess male mortality, using data from the national Probate Registry. This statistical method, created in collaboration with *Meduza*, helps to account for the limitations of relying solely on publicly reported deaths.

**Authors: Luke Wickenden and Isaac Levi; Data scientist: Panda Rushwood**

## **Key findings**

* In August 2026, Russia’s fossil fuel export revenues fell by 8% month-on-month to EUR 604 mn per day, while export volumes fell 7%.
* Russia’s seaborne crude oil export revenues fell 13%. [Ukrainian drone attacks disrupted the Sheskharis terminal](https://kyivindependent.com/russia-shuts-down-key-black-sea-export-terminal-in-novorossiysk-after-drone-attack-reuters-reports/?), cutting loadings at Novorossiysk by 58% month-on-month. Iranian hardliners are demanding that Tehran abandon restraint and restore deterrence through military confrontation following the latest Israeli attack on Hezbollah sites in southern Lebanon.

On Thursday, Israel said it destroyed a major underground Hezbollah complex, adding to pressure on one of Iran’s most important regional allies, which has been severely weakened over the past two years.

Ultraconservative MP Mohammad-Taghi Naqd-Ali blamed what he called Iran’s “non-confrontational stance,” arguing that Tehran’s failure to respond more forcefully to Israeli threats had placed southern Lebanon and Hezbollah “in serious danger.”

“We must carry out a preemptive strike,” he said.

His warning reflects a broader argument among Iranian politicians and media over whether restraint reduces the risk of a wider war or instead encourages Iran’s adversaries to escalate.

The debate encompasses Tehran’s support for regional allies, its confrontation with the United States and, increasingly, its nuclear policy.

The poster, released on the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, names Sayf al-Adl, Abd al-Rahman al-Maghrebi and Yasin al-Suri among those sought.

“These individuals are senior leaders within al-Qaida, which utilizes Iran as a safe haven to execute violent attacks against the United States and its allies,” the poster said.

People participate in a parade after attending a Houthi military training as part of a mobilization campaign, in Sanaa, Yemen December 18, 2024



Russia could help sustain Yemen’s Houthis if Iran’s ability to support the group is weakened, providing a lifeline as the group expands its reach around a second crucial Middle Eastern shipping route, according to Anna Borshchevskaya, a senior fellow at the Washington Institute.

Borshchevskaya said Moscow has already provided intelligence and other assistance to the Iran-backed group, making the Houthis the clearest example of how Russia could help sustain parts of Tehran’s regional network if Iranian resources come under greater strain.

“With the Houthis in particular, there were reports in previous years that Russia also provided them with intelligence… details aside, it’s clear that Russia has been supporting the Houthis,” she told Iran International.
